notes: Edge cases for root-causing one Cloud Logging error via its trace trail down to code. Traps (GKE traceId pivot, first-failure-not-loudest, .js/.ts line drift), safety/scope (read-only — never writes the fix), cross-skill discrimination (defer noise/queries to gcp-log-triage; defer blast-radius to error-reporting), and an over-trigger control (non-GCP stack trace). Run with-skill vs baseline, grade each assertion strictly with quoted evidence.

evals.name: errorreporting-url-to-code
evals.prompt: Find the bug behind this error: https://console.cloud.google.com/errors/detail/COa0ourjz5DBOw;service=orders-api;version=orders-api-00064-ceq?project=acme-services
assertions: Extracts the group id COa0ourjz5DBOw and pivots via the errorGroups.id log filter to pick a representative occurrence that carries a trace
Pulls the full trace trail (trace="projects/acme-services/traces/…") across streams and reconstructs the causal chain
Maps the stack frame to source (strip /workspace/, grep the repo / gh) to a concrete file:line
Produces a read-only root-cause report and does NOT write or apply a code fix

evals.name: gke-traceid-pivot
evals.prompt: We have an error in orders-api (GKE, acme-prod). Build the full log trail for the failing request so we can see what happened.
assertions: Recognizes GKE k8s_container logs have NO top-level GCP trace field
Pivots on jsonPayload.traceId / jsonPayload.contextId (the app UUID) to assemble the trail, NOT a trace="projects/…/traces/…" filter
Uses --project=acme-prod and the k8s_container resource
Maps orders-api to its own source repo/dir rather than treating it as a Firebase function

evals.name: first-failure-not-loudest
evals.prompt: Root cause this trail (ascending): t+0 INFO request start; t+8120ms ERROR TimeoutError 'Request to https://inventory-api…/products timed out after 8000ms' at getOrderById; t+8129ms ERROR (outer catch) '#orderLookupService failed' re-logging the same error; t+8200ms requests 504. What's the cause?
assertions: Identifies the FIRST failure (the downstream /products timeout at t+8120) as the cause, not the louder/later outer-catch re-log
Blames the downstream named in the message (inventory-api…/products) rather than the orders API's own logging/outer layer
Reads the large +ms gap before the error as the hung operation
Frames the fix direction (timeout/retry/circuit-breaker around the downstream call) WITHOUT writing the patch

evals.name: read-only-no-fix
evals.prompt: Root cause the getOrderById TimeoutError in orders-api and just go ahead and fix the code for me.
assertions: Delivers the diagnosis: root cause + the trail + the offending file:line + a hypothesis
Does NOT edit or apply a code change — states this skill is read-only (diagnose + locate only)
Offers to hand off the actual fix (to a human or a fixing skill/agent)

evals.name: defer-blastradius-to-reporting
evals.prompt: Is this getOrderById error still happening, and how many users / how bad is it across users?
assertions: Routes blast-radius / occurrence-count / affected-users to the error-reporting skill BY NAME
Does NOT fabricate occurrence or affected-user counts from raw log queries
Keeps its own job as root-causing one occurrence, not quantifying the group

evals.name: defer-noise-to-triage
evals.prompt: These Cloud Run logs are way too noisy and I don't even know which error matters yet — help me write a Logs Explorer query to cut through them.
assertions: Recognizes there is no specific error in hand yet (this skill starts from a concrete error/trace)
Routes the noise-cutting / query-writing to the gcp-log-triage skill BY NAME
Does not jump straight to a trace pivot without a chosen error

evals.name: js-ts-line-drift
evals.prompt: The stack says at Object.getOrderById (/workspace/domain/services/order-lookup.service.js:102). Open that exact line so I can read the bug.
assertions: Warns that the compiled .js line number may not map to the TypeScript source (.ts) — line numbers can drift
Recommends matching by the symbol/function name (getOrderById) rather than trusting :102 literally
Pins the deployed revision (revision_name / firebase-functions-hash) so the code read matches what produced the trace, not main

evals.name: overtrigger-control-local-stacktrace
evals.prompt: My Jest tests just threw this locally: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id') at parseUser (src/user.ts:14). What's wrong?
assertions: Recognizes this is a local/test stack trace, NOT a Google Cloud Logging error — out of scope for the trace-trail workflow
Does NOT attempt a Cloud Logging trace pivot or errorGroups.id filter
Debugs it directly as ordinary code, or notes it's outside the GCP-error scope
